t: Should you list a Bali villa exclusively or with every agent?
s: Open listings feel safer and usually sell for less. The reason is what an agent will and will not spend money on.
b:
Sellers in Bali overwhelmingly choose open listings — giving the property to six or eight agents at once — on the theory that more agents means more buyers. The outcome is usually the opposite, and the mechanism is worth understanding before you decide.

   What each one means

  Open listing.   Any agent may market the property. Whoever brings the buyer earns the commission. No agent has any protected position.

  Exclusive listing.   One agency markets the property for a defined period, commonly three to six months, and earns the commission on any sale in that window regardless of who introduces the buyer.

There is no licensing regime for real estate agents in Indonesia, so neither arrangement carries the professional obligations it would in Australia or the UK. Whatever protection you have comes from the contract you sign, and nothing else.

   Why open listings underperform

An agent's marketing budget goes where the return is predictable.

On an open listing, an agent who spends USD 800 on photography, drone footage, a video walkthrough and paid placement has a meaningful chance of another agency closing the buyer those assets attracted. The rational response is to spend nothing: put it on the website with the owner's phone photos, and wait for an enquiry that happens to land.

That is exactly what happens. Look at almost any open listed Bali villa and you will find four agencies carrying the same six mediocre photographs.

Meanwhile the property appears at four slightly different prices, because each agency adds its own margin or negotiates independently. A buyer who sees the same villa at USD 340,000, USD 355,000 and USD 365,000 concludes the seller is not serious, and opens at USD 300,000.

The third effect is that nobody owns the sale. No agent qualifies buyers properly, follows up, or manages the negotiation, because the effort might benefit a competitor.

   What an exclusive buys you

A budget. An agent with a protected position will commission proper p

t: How do you plan an exit from Bali property?
s: Your buyer pool is decided on the day you purchase, not the day you list. Almost nobody models this and it is where returns are actually realised.
b:
A return is not realised until the money is back. In Bali, getting it back is the hardest part of the transaction and the part nobody models.

   Your buyer pool is set at purchase

The day you buy, you determine who can buy it from you.

A   USD 250,000 three bedroom in Pererenan on a long lease   has hundreds of plausible buyers at any moment. It is the most traded product in Bali.

A   USD 900,000 five bedroom   has perhaps a dozen, and they are not all looking this year.

A   USD 400,000 villa with eleven years remaining   has almost nobody, because the arithmetic only works at a price the seller will not accept.

A   property with no PBG, or in a zone that does not permit letting  , is unsaleable to anyone doing due diligence, which means it is saleable only to someone who is not.

None of that changes between purchase and sale. It is fixed on day one, and it is the single most predictable thing about your eventual exit.

   How long it actually takes

Under USD 500,000 with a long term in a good area: three to nine months.

USD 500,000 to USD 750,000: six to eighteen months.

Above USD 750,000: twelve to twenty four months, frequently at a discount to asking.

On a leasehold, the term runs down for every month of that. A villa that takes eighteen months to sell is a villa that lost eighteen months of term while it sat, which compresses the price further. The wait is not neutral; it is a cost that compounds.

   The four exits

  Sell the remaining lease.   The normal route. Requires the deed to permit assignment, and where landowner consent is needed, that consent has a price set at the moment you have a buyer waiting. Sort this out before you list, not during.

  Sell the company.   If the property is held in a PT PMA, you can sell the shares rather than the asset. That can be cleaner and faster for the right buyer, and it narrows the pool to buyers willing to take on an Indonesian company with its history and liabilities. Get the accounts clean well in advan

t: Can you study in Indonesia on a student visa?
s: Sponsored by the institution, not by you, and it does not permit work. The language-school route is the one foreigners in Bali actually use.
b:
The student route is a legitimate residency path that is less used by foreigners in Bali than it could be, partly because people do not realise what qualifies.

   What it is

A stay permit sponsored by an   accredited Indonesian educational institution   for the duration of a course of study.

It covers formal education — universities, schools, and accredited language and vocational programmes — and depends entirely on the institution being recognised and willing to sponsor.

   Who actually uses it

  Degree students   at Indonesian universities, including at Udayana in Bali.

  Language students   on serious Bahasa Indonesia programmes at accredited institutions. This is the route most relevant to adults who want to be here legitimately while learning the language.

  Research students   and those on exchange arrangements.

  Vocational and arts students   — traditional music, dance, crafts — at recognised institutions, which is a genuine and underused category in Bali specifically.

  Children of foreign residents   attending Indonesian schools, although dependants of a KITAS holder are usually covered through a family permit instead.

   What it requires

  An accredited sponsoring institution   willing to act. This is the first and hardest step, and not every institution advertising courses to foreigners is in a position to sponsor a permit.

  Acceptance onto a course  , with documentation.

  Ministry approval   through the education pathway in addition to the immigration process.

  Financial evidence   and accommodation documentation.

  Post arrival reporting  , including registration and an SKTT.

The process is slower than most permit routes because it runs through two ministries rather than one. Allow considerably more time than you expect.

   What it does not permit

  Work.   A student permit authorises study. Employment, freelancing for Indonesian clients, or running a business operationally all require separate authorisation.

This catches people

t: Is Echo Beach a good place to buy?
s: The northern end of Canggu, surf-led rather than cafe-led, slightly cheaper and with a different guest entirely.
b:
Echo Beach — Pantai Batu Mejan — is where Canggu stops being about cafes and starts being about waves. It sits at the northern end of the strip, just before the Pererenan river mouth.

   What Echo Beach is

A black sand beach with a consistent reef bottom wave that is more serious than Batu Bolong's, a row of beachfront restaurants and bars facing the break, and residential land running back inland.

The atmosphere is different from Batu Bolong a kilometre south. Less dense, less relentless, more surf oriented. The crowd skews toward people who came for the wave rather than the coworking.

It is walkable in a limited sense — the beachfront strip itself is — but the surrounding residential areas are a scooter ride from most things.

   The market

Land here is cheaper than Batu Bolong and Berawa, and there is more of it, particularly as you move back from the beach and toward the river.

Stock is a mix of older properties on generous plots, newer villa developments, and some beachfront commercial. Plot sizes inland are better than central Canggu, which matters for delivering a proper pool within the KDB limit.

Lease terms at a given budget run longer than the Canggu core, frequently by five to ten years, which is the main commercial argument for the area.

   Rental performance

Good, with a surf weighted guest profile.

Surf travellers book around swell rather than school holidays, which means Echo Beach fills some weeks that the rest of Canggu does not. Repeat rates are high and direct booking is more common than in the cafe driven areas.

There is also solid family and group demand, drawn by larger properties and lower density than Berawa.

Nomad long stay demand exists but is thinner than Batu Bolong's, because the working infrastructure is concentrated further south. The quiet months are correspondingly quieter.

Properties that perform are three and four bedrooms with proper pools and outdoor space, and anything with a genuine view of the break. Small units c

t: How does a multiple entry visa work?
s: Two different numbers govern it, and confusing them is how people overstay without ever intending to.
b:
If you come to Indonesia several times a year, the multiple entry visa is the permit that fits, and it is consistently overlooked by people repeatedly buying visas on arrival.

   What it is

A   visit visa valid for an extended period   — commonly one, two or five years depending on the type — permitting   multiple entries   during that validity, with each individual stay limited to a defined number of days.

The critical distinction: the visa's validity is not the length of any single stay. A visa valid for five years with a sixty day per entry limit does not let you stay for five years. It lets you enter repeatedly, for up to sixty days each time, across five years.

   The categories

  Tourism.   For repeated leisure visits.

  Business.   For meetings, negotiations, site visits, conferences and exhibitions — the same scope as a single entry business visit visa, with repeated entries.

  Family visit.   For visiting family in Indonesia.

Requirements vary by category and typically include a sponsor or guarantor in Indonesia, financial evidence, and supporting documentation explaining the purpose.

   Who it suits

  Property owners who visit several times a year.   This is the obvious case and it is underused. Someone who comes four times a year for two or three weeks is a much better fit for a multiple entry visa than for four separate visas on arrival, and it removes the recurring extension anxiety.

  People doing business across the region   who pass through Indonesia repeatedly.

  Anyone with family here   visiting regularly.

  People who buy a visa on arrival every few months.   Repeated consecutive VOA use attracts attention, and immigration officers can and do decline entry to people who appear to be living in Indonesia on consecutive tourist visas. A multiple entry visa is the correct instrument for genuine repeat visiting and removes that friction.

   What it does not do

  It does not permit work.   It is a visit visa. Meetings and inspections yes

t: How do you prepare a Bali villa for sale?
s: The paperwork takes longer than the presentation and matters more. Start it three months before you list.
b:
Most Bali sales that fall over do so at the document stage, weeks after a price was agreed, when a buyer's notary finds something the seller could have fixed months earlier. Preparing to sell here is mostly a paperwork exercise.

   Start with the documents, three months out

  Find the original certificate.   Not a copy. If it is with a notary, a bank or a family member, retrieve it now. If it is lost, replacement takes months and will stop a sale dead.

  Check the land office record matches.   Name, area, boundaries, encumbrances. Discrepancies between the certificate and the register are more common than buyers assume and take time to resolve.

  Bring PBB current.   Arrears transfer with the land, and a buyer's notary will find them. Clear them and keep the receipts.

  Locate the PBG and SLF.   If the building exists and these do not, you have a choice: regularise before listing, or discount for it. Regularising is usually cheaper than the discount a buyer will demand, and much cheaper than losing the sale at week six.

  Read your own lease, if you are selling a leasehold.   Specifically whether it permits assignment, whether the landowner's consent is required, and on what terms. If consent is needed, get it in principle before you list. A seller who discovers mid sale that the landowner wants a fee to consent has lost their negotiating position entirely.

  Resolve anything outstanding.   Boundary disagreements, unpaid contractors, disputes with neighbours over access. All of it surfaces in due diligence.

   Then the numbers

If the property has been rented, a buyer will want to see performance, and vague claims reduce the price rather than raise it.

Assemble two to three years of occupancy and revenue by month, the actual operating costs, the management agreement, and tax filings. A seller who produces this credibly commands a meaningfully better price than one who says the villa "does about USD 60,000 a year".

If the numbers are poor, you have a decisi

t: What happens in your first year owning a Bali villa?
s: The gap between the projection and the first twelve months is where most owners learn what they bought. Here is the sequence.
b:
Almost every disappointing Bali investment looks fine on paper and goes wrong in the same order.

   Months 1 to 3: setup costs you did not model

Furnishing to rental standard runs USD 25,000 to 45,000 for a three bedroom villa. Photography, listing setup, staff hiring, utility connections and electrical capacity upgrades all land here.

If the property needed repairs a survey would have found, they land here too.

   Months 3 to 6: the listing does not perform

A new listing has no reviews and no ranking. Platforms surface established properties first.

Expect occupancy materially below the area average while the first ten reviews accumulate. Owners who modelled year one at stabilised occupancy run short of working capital around month eight.

This is normal and it is the most commonly omitted assumption in every projection you will be shown.

   Months 6 to 9: the cost base becomes real

Staff with BPJS at roughly 14 percent and the THR month. Platform commission. Management fees plus everything billed separately. Utilities that rise with occupancy. Laundry and consumables scaling with turnover. Pool chemicals, garden, repairs.

Gross revenue looks fine. What arrives is a different number.

   Months 9 to 12: the first real maintenance

Humidity, salt and UV work fast. Soft goods degrade in one to three years. Something in the pool plant or the air conditioning fails.

If you did not provision a sinking fund, this comes out of the year's profit.

   What separates owners who do well

  They budgeted 30 to 40 percent above the purchase price for setup and buffer
  They modelled year one well below stabilised occupancy
  They own their own listing account, not the manager's
  They have someone genuinely present and responsive
  They provisioned a sinking fund from month one

   The single most useful thing to do before buying

Get twelve consecutive months of actual operating statements from a genuinely comparable property. Not a projection, not an average, stateme

t: How do you make money on a Bali leasehold?
s: A wasting asset can still produce a return, but only if the income clears the decay. That arithmetic is the whole discipline.
b:
A leasehold loses value every year by design. Making money on one means the income has to outrun that decay, and most projections never mention it.

   The core arithmetic

Two things happen simultaneously:

  The asset decays.   A 30 year lease with 30 years left is worth more than the same lease with 20 left. The decline accelerates as the term shortens, because your buyer inherits the expiry.

  The property produces income.   Rent, nightly or annual.

Your actual return is the income   minus   the value the lease shed that year. A villa yielding 6 percent net on a lease losing 4 percent of its value annually is not a 6 percent investment.

Almost nobody models the second half.

   The four ways money is actually made

  One: income that clears the decay.   Requires strong, licensed, differentiated performance. Generic villas in oversupplied corridors frequently do not manage it.

  Two: buy long, sell shorter but still long.   Buy at 30 years, sell at 22. The decay between those points is shallower than between 12 and 4. Most of the value loss happens at the end.

  Three: improve the asset.   Buy a tired leasehold, refurbish, and capture the gap between the discount you bought at and what a functioning property commands.

  Four: fix the paperwork.   Buy a leasehold discounted for a weak extension clause, missing permits or a licence problem, then resolve it. This is the most reliable value creation available in this market and the least attempted, because it requires knowing what is broken.

   What kills leasehold returns

  A short remaining term, bought at near freehold pricing
    Prioritas   rather than   jaminan   on the extension
  Extension rights that do not pass to your buyer
  Assignment requiring unqualified consent, or an uncapped fee
  No operating licence, so the income you modelled cannot lawfully exist
  The building reverting at expiry with no compensation clause

   The honest rule

  Buy term, sell term.   Your entry price should reflect th

t: Is Balangan or Padang Padang worth buying?
s: Two of the best beaches on the Bukit, both constrained by access, water and the setback rules that have already bitten nearby.
b:
Balangan and Padang Padang are among the best beaches in Bali and two of the more difficult places to buy well.

   What they are

  Balangan   is a long white sand beach below a limestone cliff on the western Bukit, with a left hand reef break and a row of warungs along the sand. Wider and less crowded than most of the peninsula's beaches.

  Padang Padang   sits south of it, a small cove reached through a gap in the rock, with one of the most famous waves in Indonesia just offshore. The beach itself is tiny and gets very busy.

Both sit below clifftops carrying residential land with ocean views, and behind that the interior Bukit at Pecatu.

The guest is surf led, loyal and repeat heavy, booking around swell rather than school holidays.

   The setback issue

This is the first thing to establish and the reason the area carries more risk than its appeal suggests.

The   sempadan pantai  , the coastal setback measured from the high water line, restricts building within a defined distance. Along this stretch of the Bukit, a meaningful amount of what exists on and near the cliff was built without the required permits and inside that setback.

Enforcement has tightened, and   demolition action against unpermitted cliff structures has taken place nearby at Bingin  . That is a realised outcome, not a theoretical risk.

So: a property on or into the cliff here is high risk unless you can see a valid PBG and SLF matching the structure that exists, plus confirmation from the regency that it sits outside the setback, verified by a notary you engaged. A property on the plateau set back from the edge is a much more ordinary proposition.

Marketing does not always make clear which category is being offered. Establish it before anything else.

   Access

The second constraint, and it is underrated.

Both beaches are reached by steep paths and steps. Padang Padang's access is through a narrow gap in the rock. Neither is suitable for anyone with mobility limitations, and guests ar

t: What happens if your visa expires while applying for another?
s: Switching categories leaves a window where one permit has ended and the next has not arrived. That gap is the risk.
b:
People arrive from Australia or the UK assuming Indonesia has something equivalent to a bridging visa. It broadly does not, and understanding that early prevents an expensive mistake.

   The expectation

In Australia, a bridging visa keeps you lawfully in the country while a substantive application is decided. Your existing visa expires, the bridging visa takes effect, and you remain lawful.

The UK has a comparable concept through the continuation of leave while an in time application is pending.

That mechanism creates a habit: apply before expiry and you are covered while it processes.

   The Indonesian position

  There is no general equivalent.   Lodging an extension or a new permit application does not, by itself, create a lawful status that survives the expiry of your current permit.

Some categories carry specific arrangements while a change or extension is processed, and practice varies by permit type and by office. What does not exist is a blanket rule that an application in progress protects you.

The practical consequence:   if your permit expires while an application is pending and no specific arrangement covers you, you are in overstay.   A daily fine accrues from day one, per person, and past a threshold measured in weeks it escalates to detention, deportation and a re entry ban.

Immigration does not treat "I had applied" as an answer.

   What to do instead

  Apply early, not on time.   A month to six weeks before expiry for a KITAS extension, and as soon as the window opens for a visa on arrival extension. Build in margin for a document that needs correcting and an appointment that is not available immediately.

  Confirm what covers you during processing.   Ask explicitly, for your specific permit type, what your status is while the application is pending and get the answer from immigration or a consultant rather than an agent's reassurance.

  Keep an exit option.   If a renewal is uncertain, holding a flight out before expiry removes the wors

t: Do you need an alcohol licence in Bali?
s: Serving alcohol commercially is separately licensed from your accommodation permit, and enforcement treats them as different things.
b:
Owners assume that if the property is licensed for accommodation, everything happening inside it is covered. It is not.

   Two separate permissions

  Accommodation licensing   covers selling nights.   Selling alcohol   is its own regulated activity with its own permit.

A villa that provides a stocked minibar and charges for it, or a property running a bar, is engaged in the second activity whether or not it holds the first.

   The classification layer

Alcohol sale sits within Indonesia's licensing system with its own classification, and permits differ by alcohol category and by the type of premises.

That means the permit a beach club holds is not the permit a small café needs, and neither is automatically what a villa requires.

   Where villa owners get caught

  The stocked minibar.   Provided free as hospitality is one thing. Charged for is a sale.

  Events.   Weddings and private parties where alcohol is supplied as part of a paid package.

  In villa bar service.   Staff serving drinks as a charged service.

The practical fix for many small operators is to not sell alcohol at all: let guests buy their own, or have a licensed supplier handle it. That removes the exposure entirely.

   Enforcement context

Regional authorities can issue warnings, suspend operations and close premises directly. The cost is not the penalty, it is a property carrying its full staff and maintenance base while shut.

Given the direction of regulation since Perda Bali 4/2026 and the July 2026 classification closures, assume scrutiny increases rather than relaxes.

   What to verify

  Does the business hold a valid alcohol permit for its category and premises?
  Does it cover the specific activity, retail, on premises consumption, or events?
  Is the NIB active with the right classification?
  If you are buying a venue, does the permit transfer, or sit in an entity not in the sale?

That last question applies exactly as it does to accommodation licences. A permit in a company th

t: Is Munduk worth buying in?
s: Waterfalls, coffee plantations, cool air and almost no rental market. A lifestyle purchase that should never be underwritten on yield.
b:
Munduk sits in the central highlands above the northern lakes, at altitude, where Bali is cool, green and almost entirely agricultural.

   What is there

Coffee and clove plantations, waterfalls, ridge walks, the lakes at Tamblingan and Buyan, and a small number of guesthouses and boutique retreats.

It is beautiful and it is genuinely cold at night by Bali standards, which is the whole appeal.

   The market reality

There is essentially no villa rental market here in the sense the south understands it. Guests come for one or two nights on a circuit, not for a two week villa holiday.

Land is cheap because demand is thin, not because it has been overlooked.

  Factor   Munduk  
             
  Land price   Among the lowest on the island  
  Rental demand   Very thin, short stays  
  Seasonality   Pronounced  
  Resale   Very shallow  
  Airport   Roughly 2.5 to 3 hours  
  Amenities   Minimal  
  Climate   Cool, wet, frequently misty  

   The constraints

Almost everything here is agricultural green zone, which is the first thing to verify and usually the deciding one.

Access roads are narrow and steep, which raises construction cost and limits guest access. Rain is heavier and more persistent than the coast, with real implications for damp, mould and road condition.

   Who it suits

Someone building a home or a small retreat they will run themselves, with a long horizon, no need for liquidity and no expectation of income.

It does not suit investors. There is no version of this that produces a yield comparable to the south.

   What to verify

Zoning, first and always. Access road width and gradient. Water, which is plentiful here but still parcel specific. Land stability on slopes. Realistic drive times to a hospital and the airport.

   The lakes

Tamblingan and Buyan sit in a caldera near Munduk, and Bratan with its lakeside temple is further east at Bedugul. This is protected and agricultural land almost throughout, which is why the area looks the way it d

t: Is Kuta or Legian still worth buying?
s: The original tourist strip, now the cheapest developed coastline in the south. Unfashionable is not the same as unprofitable.
b:
Kuta and Legian are where Bali tourism started, and they have been out of fashion with foreign buyers for a decade.

   What that means

Prices per are on the developed south coast are lowest here. The stock is older, the streets are denser, and the area reads as mass tourism rather than boutique.

Meanwhile it has: the airport fifteen minutes away, a long sandy beach that is genuinely good for learning to surf, the deepest concentration of budget and mid market accommodation in Indonesia, and year round demand from a market that never stopped coming.

   The investment case nobody makes

Demand here is enormous and consistent. It is simply demand at a lower price point, from Australian, domestic Indonesian and regional Asian visitors rather than from the Canggu set.

That demand is less seasonal and less fashion dependent than the west coast corridor. It also does not require a three bedroom pool villa to capture.

  Factor   Kuta / Legian  
             
  Entry price   Lowest on the developed south coast  
  Demand   High volume, lower rate  
  Seasonality   Milder than Canggu  
  Guest   Budget, family, domestic, surf schools  
  Stock   Older, dense, commercial  
  Resale   Local buyer pool as well as foreign  

   The problems, honestly

Traffic and density. Older buildings with maintenance debt. A reputation that means many foreign buyers will not look, which cuts both ways: less competition buying, fewer buyers selling.

Legian is the calmer end. Seminyak adjacent northern Legian prices closer to Seminyak.

   What to check

Building age and condition, PBG and SLF including extensions, remaining lease term, noise on the specific street, flood behaviour in wet season, and whether the licence covers what the property actually does.

   The segments that work here

  Budget and mid market accommodation.   Consistent, high volume demand that never stopped, largely ignored by foreign buyers chasing villa yields.

  Commercial frontage.   Retail and food and bever

t: What can you buy in Bali under $100,000?
s: Under a hundred thousand you are buying land, a short lease, or a small off-plan unit. Each of those is a different risk, and only one of them is usually worth it.
b:
This is the most common budget I get asked about, and the honest answer starts with what it excludes. Under USD 100,000 you are not buying a finished, licensed, income producing villa in a prime area. Anyone showing you one is either misdescribing the title, the remaining term, or the permit.

What the budget does buy is real. It is just narrower than the marketing suggests.

   The four things $100,000 actually buys

  Land, in the right regency.   An are of land — 100 square metres — runs from around USD 7,000 in Tabanan and east Bali to well over USD 60,000 in Berawa. At the lower end, a hundred thousand buys enough land to build on later. At the upper end it buys a parking space. Land is the one purchase at this budget where you are not competing with better funded buyers for the same stock.

  A short leasehold on a finished villa.   Eight to twelve years remaining, usually a one or two bedroom in Kerobokan, Umalas, Pererenan or the Bukit. The price is low precisely because the term is nearly gone. The maths only works if the rental income repays the purchase before the lease expires, with a margin. Run that number before anything else.

  A small off plan unit.   Studio or one bedroom, frequently sold as part of a complex with a rental programme attached. This is where most of the losses at this budget happen, because you are paying in instalments for something that does not exist, against a developer you cannot enforce against.

  A stake in someone else's project.   Usually presented as a "fund" or a "co ownership". Almost never worth it at this size, because the fee load eats the return and you have no control over the exit.

   The lease term problem

At this budget the single variable that decides everything is remaining term, and it is the one buyers discount hardest.

A villa with eight years left is not a cheap villa. It is a rental income stream with an end date and a demolition value building at the end of it. If it nets USD 12,000 a year and costs U

t: Should you buy in Denpasar?
s: The capital, almost entirely a local market, and the place to look if you want tenants who live here rather than visit.
b:
Denpasar is Bali's capital and its only real city: government, hospitals, universities, the main markets and roughly a million people in the wider metro area.

   Why foreign buyers ignore it

No beach, no view, no tourism. It is hot, dense and functional. Almost nothing here is marketed to foreigners.

That is exactly why the pricing is different.

   What it offers instead

  A domestic tenant market.   Professionals, students, government workers and families who live here permanently and are not affected by tourism seasonality or flight capacity.

  Hospitals.   Sanglah and the main private hospitals are here, which is why Sanur commands a premium for being close to it.

  Infrastructure.   Real services, real shops, functioning utilities.

  Price.   Substantially below anything coastal.

   The structural point

Every tourism dependent property in Bali shares one risk: arrivals. A pandemic, an ash cloud, a flight capacity constraint or a regulatory change hits all of them at once, as 2020 and 2021 demonstrated precisely.

Denpasar residential demand comes from people who live here regardless.

   The limitations

The foreign buyer pool for Denpasar is tiny, which makes resale to a foreigner hard. Yields are ordinary rather than exciting. And the ownership rules are identical, so you still cannot hold freehold.

Realistically this is a market for someone with a long Indonesian horizon, possibly through a PT PMA, rather than a lifestyle purchase.

   What to check

Zoning and permitted use, since much of Denpasar is residential rather than commercial. Flood behaviour, which is a genuine issue in parts. Title history on older parcels. And who your tenant actually is before you buy for them.

   Where people actually live

Renon holds the government quarter and the embassies, with wide streets and the most orderly housing in the city. Sanglah surrounds the main hospital. Panjer and Sesetan are ordinary residential districts where prices are lowest.

Foreign residen

t: What can you buy in Bali with $100,000 to $250,000?
s: This is the bracket where a real income property becomes possible, and also where the most overpriced off-plan units in Bali are sold.
b:
This is the busiest price band in Bali and the one with the widest gap between what is marketed and what is delivered. It is also the first bracket where a genuinely workable investment exists.

   What the range buys

  USD 100,000 to 150,000.   A two bedroom on a fifteen to twenty year lease outside the prime strip. Pererenan's edges, Kedungu, Tabanan, Ungasan, the quieter parts of Umalas. Or roughly two to four are of land in a mid tier area, which is a build project rather than a purchase.

  USD 150,000 to 200,000.   A two or three bedroom on a twenty to twenty five year lease in a decent location, or a well specified off plan two bedroom in a complex. This is where most of the off plan stock in Bali is priced, and where most of the disappointment lives.

  USD 200,000 to 250,000.   A three bedroom with pool on a twenty five year lease in Pererenan, Umalas, Kerobokan or the Bukit. Or a completed two bedroom in Berawa or Batu Bolong with a shorter term. This is the first point at which the property can plausibly cover its own costs and return capital within the term.

   The off plan concentration

More off plan units are sold in this band than in any other, and the reason is structural. A developer can build a two bedroom unit in a complex for a cost that makes a USD 180,000 sale price very profitable, and the buyer at that level is usually buying their first Bali property and has no local reference points.

The pitch is consistent: a projected yield in the low to mid teens, a rental management programme, and a payment schedule spread across construction. The yield figure is almost always gross, before management, maintenance, tax, the licence, the platform commission and vacancy. Net is commonly half the headline, sometimes less.

What I check before anything else on an off plan deal in this band:

  Whether the PBG has actually been issued, not applied for
  Who holds the land, on what title, and for how long
  What happens to your money if the build stops

t: Should you buy on Nusa Ceningan?
s: Connected to Lembongan by a yellow bridge and smaller than anywhere else foreigners buy. Every constraint on Lembongan applies harder here.
b:
Nusa Ceningan is the smallest of the three Nusa islands, joined to Lembongan by a narrow suspension bridge.

   What is there

Cliff jumping at Mahana Point, the Blue Lagoon, seaweed farms in the channel, a handful of small resorts and warungs, and very little else.

You can cross the island in fifteen minutes. That is the scale.

   The constraints, and they are sharper than Lembongan

  Constraint   Reality  
             
  Water   Very limited. Shipped or desalinated  
  Power   Dependent on the connection through Lembongan  
  Access   Boat to Lembongan, then the bridge  
  Construction   Materials arrive by boat, then cross a narrow bridge  
  Medical   None meaningful. Boat to Bali for anything serious  
  Resale   Almost nonexistent  

The bridge is the thing people underestimate. Everything that gets built here crosses a narrow span, which constrains both cost and what is practical to build.

   The demand pattern

Day visitors from Lembongan and Bali dominate. Overnight demand exists at the small resorts and is heavily seasonal and weather dependent.

Rough seas cancel crossings, which cancels arrivals. A property underwritten on mainland assumptions will not perform.

   Who this suits

Almost nobody as an investment. It suits an operator who wants to run a small property personally, on a very long horizon, with capital they will not need back.

If the appeal is the Nusa islands generally, Lembongan has better infrastructure and a slightly deeper market. Penida has more land and more visitors.

   What to verify

Water supply and its real monthly cost. Power arrangements and backup. Title, through a mainland notary you appointed. Access and construction logistics including the bridge. And honestly, who your buyer is at exit.

   Compared with the other two Nusas

  Nusa Penida   is far larger, has the famous viewpoints, takes the bulk of day trip traffic and has the most land and the most construction.

  Nusa Lembongan   is the established middle option,

t: What can you buy in Bali with $250,000 to $500,000?
s: This is where prime-area stock, long terms and genuine income properties all become available at once, and where the decision stops being about price.
b:
At this level the constraint stops being budget and becomes judgement. Almost everything is available to you. The question shifts from what you can afford to what you should want.

   What the range buys

  USD 250,000 to 350,000.   A three or four bedroom villa with pool on a twenty five to thirty year lease in Pererenan, Cemagi, Umalas, Kerobokan, Ungasan or Bingin. In Berawa or Batu Bolong the same money buys a three bedroom with a shorter term. Land of four to six are in a good corridor, or two to three are in a prime one.

  USD 350,000 to 500,000.   Four bedrooms, better land, a longer term, or a prime address. A well located Berawa or Pererenan villa on thirty years. A Bukit property with an ocean view, which is the single biggest price multiplier in Bali. Or a complete build on good land with nothing compromised.

  Around USD 500,000   you enter the range where Hak Pakai becomes a live option if you hold residency, and where a PT PMA holding HGB starts to make commercial sense rather than just being possible.

   The structure question becomes real

Below USD 250,000, almost everyone buys leasehold because the alternatives cost more to set up than they save. Above it, the three routes genuinely compete.

  Leasehold   stays the simplest and cheapest to execute, and remains a wasting asset. At thirty years and this price, that is usually fine.

  Hak Pakai   requires a KITAS or KITAP, applies to houses and apartments above a value threshold, and gives you a right registered at the land office in your own name. If you have residency and intend to live here, it is the strongest position available to a foreigner and this is the budget where it starts to apply.

  HGB through a PT PMA   gives you a registered building right held by your company, with no residency requirement, and it is the route if the property is a business. It carries capital requirements, annual accounts, tax filings and real ongoing cost. Bali closed new foreign owned villa and homestay regi

t: What does beachfront land cost in Bali?
s: The price is high, the supply is nearly fixed, and the setback rules mean a significant part of what you buy cannot be built on.
b:
Beachfront is the most misunderstood category in the Bali market, because the thing being sold and the thing buyers think they are buying are not the same.

   You cannot own the beach

The foreshore in Indonesia is state land. Nobody holds private title to the beach itself, and nobody can sell it to you.

What exists is land adjacent to the beach, subject to a coastal setback — the  sempadan pantai  — within which building is restricted or prohibited. The setback is measured from the high water line and its width varies by regency and by the specific spatial plan, commonly in the range of tens of metres.

So a beachfront parcel includes a strip you own and cannot build on. On a shallow plot that strip can be most of the land. The advertised area and the buildable area are very different numbers, and the price is usually quoted against the first.

   What it costs

Genuine beachfront land in Bali, September 2026, broadly:

  Seminyak, Petitenget, Batu Belig   — the deepest established market. Very little changes hands. When it does, prices are set privately and are the highest on the island outside of specific Bukit clifftop positions.

  Berawa, Batu Bolong, Echo Beach   — the Canggu coastal strip. Extremely tight supply, and much of what is described as beachfront is second or third row.

  Pererenan, Seseh, Cemagi, Kedungu   — the growth corridor. Coastal land here is where most current beachfront transactions actually happen, at a substantial discount to Canggu proper.

  Tabanan and the west coast   — materially cheaper, black sand, thinner rental demand, and the corridor most likely to reprice upward over the next decade.

  Bukit clifftop   — not beachfront in the technical sense but priced above it, because a protected ocean view from a cliff is the scarcest position in Bali and is not subject to the same setback problem.

  North and east Bali   — Lovina, Amed, Candidasa. Coastal land at a fraction of southern prices, with a rental market small enough to tr

t: What can you buy in Bali for over $500,000?
s: Above half a million the market is thin, the buyers are few and the exit is the hardest part of the deal. That changes what you should be looking at.
b:
Above USD 500,000 the Bali market gets thin in both directions. Fewer properties, and far fewer buyers when you come to sell. That asymmetry should shape everything about how you buy at this level.

   What the money buys

  USD 500,000 to 750,000.   A large villa on a long lease in a prime area, a clifftop or ocean view property on the Bukit, or substantial land with a complete high specification build. Five bedrooms in Pererenan or Umalas on thirty years. A serious Uluwatu view property.

  USD 750,000 to 1.5 million.   Estate scale land, a small boutique development, a beachfront position, or a property that functions as a business rather than a villa. At this level you are frequently buying a commercial operation with a villa attached.

  Above USD 1.5 million.   Hotels, resorts, land banks, and developments. A different market with different buyers, largely transacted privately rather than listed.

   The exit is the whole problem

A USD 250,000 villa has hundreds of plausible buyers in Bali at any time. A USD 900,000 villa has perhaps a dozen, and they are not all looking this year.

This is the single most underestimated factor at the top of this market. Properties above USD 750,000 routinely sit for twelve to twenty four months, and the successful sales are usually at a meaningful discount to asking. Meanwhile the lease term is running down, which compresses the price further every year you hold it unsold.

Two consequences follow. First, buy at a price that assumes a slow, discounted exit, not a fast one. Second, prefer properties with an income stream strong enough that holding for two years while you sell is comfortable rather than painful.

   Freehold equivalent structures matter more here

At this value, the structure carries real weight because the amount at risk is large and the exit is slow.

A thirty year lease on a USD 900,000 property loses roughly USD 30,000 of value a year to term decay alone, before any market movement. That is a significant a

t: How many bedrooms should a Bali villa have?
s: Revenue per bedroom falls as you add bedrooms, but total revenue rises and costs do not rise as fast. Where that crosses over is the whole decision.
b:
This is the most consequential design decision in a Bali rental villa, and it gets made on instinct far more often than on arithmetic.

   The pattern in the numbers

Nightly rate does not scale linearly with bedrooms. A one bedroom might achieve USD 90 a night. Two bedrooms does not get USD 180; it gets around USD 150. Three gets roughly USD 210, four around USD 280, five around USD 340.

Per bedroom, that is USD 90, USD 75, USD 70, USD 70, USD 68. Revenue per bedroom falls and then flattens.

But costs do not follow the same curve. One pool, one kitchen, one garden, one villa manager and broadly one cleaning team serve four bedrooms nearly as easily as they serve two. The fixed cost base is the villa, not the rooms.

So net income per bedroom improves as you add bedrooms, even though gross per bedroom falls. That is the argument for building larger, and it holds up to a point.

   Where it stops holding

Occupancy is the counterweight, and it moves the opposite way.

One and two bedroom villas in Bali serve couples and small groups, which is the deepest and most consistent demand pool in the market. They book year round, they book late, and they fill shoulder season.

Four, five and six bedroom villas serve families and groups. That demand is real and it pays well, but it is lumpier, more seasonal, books further ahead, and collapses harder in a quiet month. A five bedroom at sixty percent occupancy earns less than a three bedroom at eighty.

The other constraint is land. Bedrooms need footprint, and KDB limits how much of your plot you may build on. Adding a fifth bedroom often means a smaller pool or losing the garden, which are the two things that photograph the property and set the rate.

   The practical answer

  Three bedrooms is the most reliable configuration in Bali.   It serves couples travelling together, small families and groups of friends, which is the widest demand pool available. It sits inside most plot sizes without compromising the pool. It cost

t: Is Berawa a good place to buy property?
s: Berawa has the highest occupancy in Canggu and the highest land prices. Whether it works depends entirely on what term you can get.
b:
Berawa is the most commercially developed part of Canggu and, by most measures, the strongest rental market on the island. It is also where the gap between rental performance and purchase price is narrowest.

   What Berawa is now

A dense strip running from the Canggu Shortcut down to Berawa Beach, with Atlas, Finns, La Brisa and a continuous run of restaurants, gyms, clinics and co working along it. It has the infrastructure of a small town and the traffic to match.

The guest profile is broad: couples, families, groups, digital nomads on longer stays, and a substantial repeat market. That breadth is what produces the occupancy, and it is the single strongest argument for the area.

   The numbers

Land in Berawa is among the most expensive in Bali outside of Seminyak's core and specific Bukit clifftop positions. Prices per are here have roughly doubled over five years and the corridor is effectively built out, which means new supply arrives by replacing existing buildings rather than by expanding.

Rental performance is correspondingly strong. Well run villas here achieve high occupancy across a longer season than most of Bali, with less of a February collapse than areas depending on a narrower guest type.

The problem is what that does to the purchase decision. High land price plus high rental income does not automatically mean a good investment. It means the return is already priced in, and the variable left to you is the lease term.

   The term problem

Because land is expensive, the leases available in Berawa at a given budget are shorter than they would be elsewhere.

At USD 250,000, Berawa offers a three bedroom with perhaps fifteen to eighteen years remaining. The same money in Pererenan or Cemagi offers the same house with twenty five to thirty. Berawa's higher income does not close a ten year gap in term. It rarely comes close.

t: How do you set the nightly rate for a Bali villa?
s: Most owners price off the listing prices of neighbours, which are not what those villas achieve. Here is the method that actually works.
b:
Pricing is the highest leverage thing an owner controls and the thing most owners spend the least time on. A twelve percent improvement in average rate is a twelve percent improvement in revenue with no additional cost, and it is routinely available.

   Stop pricing off listed rates

The most common method in Bali is to look at three similar villas nearby, see what they list at, and price just under.

That fails because listed rates are asking prices. A villa listing at USD 250 might be averaging USD 165 after discounts, long stay rates, direct bookings and empty nights. Pricing "just under" its listing means pricing well above what it actually achieves, which is why so many well presented Bali villas sit at forty percent occupancy wondering why.

What you want is achieved rate, not listed rate. You get it by watching a set of comparable villas' availability calendars over six to eight weeks and noting which dates fill and at what price. Tedious, and it is the only reliable source.

   Build the rate from the calendar, not the year

Bali does not have one rate. It has at least four.

  Peak   — July, August, and roughly 20 December to 5 January. Demand exceeds supply. Rates run forty to seventy percent above base, minimum stays go to three to five nights, and you should be close to full.

  High   — May, June, September, early October. Strong demand, rates ten to twenty five percent above base, occupancy in the eighties for a well run property.

  Base   — March, April, mid October, November.

  Low   — late January, February. The rainy season trough. Rates fifteen to twenty five percent below base, and this is where occupancy is won or lost.

Setting one rate for the year means you undercharge for a third of it and overcharge for another third. That single error costs more than most owners' entire management fee.

   Work out your floor before anything else

Your floor is the rate below which a booking costs you money.

t: What is property like in Petitenget and Batu Belig?
s: The strip between Seminyak and Canggu has the amenity of both and the traffic of neither. It is the most underrated position in the south.
b:
Petitenget and Batu Belig occupy the stretch between Seminyak's northern edge and the Canggu river mouth. They are frequently skipped by buyers who look at Seminyak and then at Canggu and never stop in between.

   What the area is

Petitenget runs north from Seminyak along Jalan Petitenget, a continuous run of established restaurants, beach clubs and hotels. Batu Belig continues north to the beach of the same name, becoming lower density and more residential as it goes.

The character is more grown up than Canggu and less relentless than Seminyak's centre. The guest profile skews older and higher spending: couples, families, people who want walkable dining without the scooter density of Berawa.

Beach access at Batu Belig is genuinely good, and the sunset stretch here is one of the better ones in the south.

   Why it is underrated

Three things.

  Location.   It sits between the two strongest demand centres in Bali with road access to both. A guest can reach Seminyak's restaurants and Canggu's beach clubs in ten to fifteen minutes.

  Established infrastructure.   Unlike the northern Canggu corridor, this area was built out years ago. Roads, drainage and utilities are in a different condition to what you find in Pererenan or Seseh. That matters more than buyers expect, particularly in the rainy season.

  Pricing.   Land here is cheaper than Seminyak's core and, on some streets, cheaper than Berawa, for a position with comparable amenity and better infrastructure.

   What the market looks like

Stock is largely existing villas rather than new development, because the area is built out. That has an advantage and a cost: what you buy exists and can be inspected, but new build opportunities are rare and land rarely trades.

Villas here are often ten to twenty years old. The build quality of that generation is variable and renovation is frequently part of the purchase. Budget for it rather than discovering it.

t: Villa, apartment or townhouse in Bali?
s: The three property types carry different titles, different licences and completely different exit markets. The building is the least important difference.
b:
Buyers compare these three on layout and price. The differences that actually matter are legal and structural, and they show up years later at the exit.

   Villa

A standalone building on its own plot, with its own pool in most cases, and its own land right underneath it.

  Title.   Leasehold over the land, Hak Pakai if you hold residency and the value threshold is met, or HGB held by a PT PMA. You control the land right directly.

  Control.   Total. You decide on renovation, management, pricing and when to sell. No committee, no service charge, no shared decisions.

  Income.   The highest gross and net of the three, and the widest range of outcomes. A well run villa outperforms everything. A badly run one underperforms an apartment.

  Costs.   The highest. Pool maintenance, garden, staff, structural upkeep, insurance. Expect fifteen to twenty five percent of gross revenue before management fees.

  Exit.   The deepest resale market in Bali by a large margin. Villas are what buyers come here looking for.

   Apartment

A unit within a building, usually with shared facilities and a body corporate running them.

  Title.   Strata title —  Hak Milik atas Satuan Rumah Susun  — over the unit, with the land held collectively. Foreigners may hold strata title over an apartment subject to a minimum value threshold, and in practice most foreign apartment ownership in Bali runs through leasehold or a company anyway.

  Control.   Limited. A building committee makes decisions about the common property, the service charge is set collectively, and your ability to renovate is constrained.

  Income.   Lower gross than a villa of equivalent value, but lower costs and much lower management burden. Occupancy is often higher because the price point serves a bigger market.

  Costs.   Service charge, which is predictable and unavoidable, plus a sinking fund for building works. Considerably simpler than running a villa.

t: Can you earn passive income from Bali property?
s: It is income, and it is not passive. Knowing exactly how much attention it needs is the difference between a good year and a bad one.
b:
"Passive income" is the phrase that sells most Bali property, and it is the one I would push back on hardest. The income is real. The passivity is not, and the properties that perform are the ones whose owners understood that from the start.

   What it actually takes

A short let villa in Bali is a hospitality business with one unit. Somebody has to handle:

Pricing across four distinct seasons. Guest communication, often across time zones and at short notice. Check in and check out. Cleaning and laundry between every stay. Pool chemistry, weekly at minimum. Garden maintenance in a climate that grows things fast. Staff management, scheduling and payroll. Repairs, which in a humid tropical environment arrive more often than owners expect. Platform listings, photography refreshes, review management. Licensing and tax filings. Restocking consumables.

You can pay someone to do all of it. You cannot make it stop needing to be done, and you cannot fully delegate the judgement about whether it is being done well.

   The management fee reality

A full service villa manager in Bali charges fifteen to twenty five percent of gross revenue, sometimes more for smaller properties. Some structures add a fixed monthly fee on top, and some mark up maintenance.

At twenty percent of a USD 70,000 gross, that is USD 14,000 a year. Add maintenance, utilities, staff, licensing, platform commission and tax and you are commonly at forty to fifty percent of gross before you see anything.

That is not a criticism of managers. Running a villa well is genuinely difficult and the good ones earn it. It is a correction to the arithmetic, because most projections handed to buyers do not include it properly.

   Where the passive version breaks

  The manager underperforms and you do not notice.   The most common failure. Occupancy drifts from seventy five to fifty five percent over two years, revenue falls, and nobody tells you because the manager's incentive is the easy life, not the marginal

t: Who actually books Bali villas?
s: Different parts of Bali serve different guests with different booking behaviour. Buying in the wrong area for your property type costs you occupancy.
b:
Bali is not one rental market. It is several, and they behave differently enough that a villa which fills easily in one area would struggle two corridors away.

   The main guest groups

  Australians.   The largest and most consistent source market, and the most seasonal. School holidays drive their calendar hard: late June through July, late September, and the December January peak. They book families and groups, favour Seminyak, Canggu, Uluwatu and increasingly the Bukit, and they return. Repeat rates are high.

  Europeans.   Longer stays, less concentrated in school holidays, and stronger in the May to September window when Europe is warm but Bali is dry. They skew toward Ubud, the Bukit and Canggu, and they research more before booking, which means your listing quality matters more with this group.

  Asian regional travellers   from Singapore, Malaysia, Korea, Japan and increasingly China and India. Shorter stays, often long weekends, and a strong preference for Seminyak, Nusa Dua and the developed south. Higher expectations around service and facilities, and much less interested in a remote villa down a dirt road.

  Digital nomads and long stayers.   Concentrated in Canggu, Pererenan and Ubud. Monthly bookings, price sensitive, care about internet and workspace far more than pool size. They fill low season, which is precisely when you need filling.

  Surf travellers.   The Bukit — Uluwatu, Bingin, Padang Padang, Balangan — and the Canggu to Seseh coast. Season driven by swell rather than holidays, which means they fill different weeks than everyone else. Loyal, repeat heavy, and often book direct.

  Wellness and retreat visitors.   Ubud primarily. Book through programmes and retreats rather than platforms, which changes how you reach them entirely.
